c.title: Proposal 2026-1
c.pre: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
c.q: Shall a convention of elected delegates be convened in 2027 to draft a general revision of the State Constitution for presentation to the state’s voters for their approval or rejection?

c.title: Proposal 2026-2
c.pre: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
c.q:
The proposal would:

• Prohibit regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 annually in government contracts, and people and organizations with substantial connections to these utilities/contractors from making direct or indirect campaign contributions to those who run for or hold offices that impact them.

• Expand laws regulating spending on political communications, including those requiring disclosing donor information, to apply to communications clearly identifying candidates or ballot questions, even if they do not expressly advocate voting for/against them.

• Expressly apply the law requiring disclosure of who paid for political communications to internet political communications.

Should this proposal be adopted?

c.title: PROPOSAL FOR FIRE AND AMBULANCE MILLAGE
c.q: Shall Evangeline Township impose an increase of up to 1 mill ($1 per $1,000 of taxable value), in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive for the purpose of providing fire and ambulance services in the Township? If approved and levied, this millage would raise an estimated $122,253 in the first year that the millage is levied, of which a portion may be distributed to such other local units of government or others as the Township Board determines appropriate.

c.title: PROPOSAL TO APPROVE RENEWAL OF FIRE PROTECTION SERVICES MILLAGE
c.q: Shall the expired previous voted millage increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Section 6 of the Michigan Constitution in the Township of Norwood of 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), which has been reduced to .9850 mills by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed and increased to the originally voted 1 mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for four (4) years (2026 through 2029 inclusive) for the provision of fire protection services in the Township, raising in the first year an estimated $72,000?

c.title: Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District Special Education Millage Renewal Proposal
c.q:
This proposal will allow the intermediate school district to continue to levy special education millage previously approved by the electors.

Shall the currently authorized millage rate limitation of 0.6231 mill ($0.6231 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property in Cheboygan-Otsego-Presque Isle Educational Service District, Michigan, to provide funds for the education of students with a disability, be renewed for a period of 6 years, 2027 to 2032, inclusive; the estimate of the revenue the intermediate school district will collect if the millage is approved and levied in 2027 is approximately $2,992,734 from local property taxes authorized herein (this is a renewal of millage that will expire with the 2026 tax levy)?

c.title: FIRE PROTECTION SERVICES
c.q: Shall Hayes Township impose an increase of up to 0.4 mills ($0.40) per $1,000.00 of taxable value in the tax limitation under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it three years from 2026 through 2028 inclusive, for fire protection services for the Township, which 0.4 Mills increase will raise an estimated $129,601.09 in the first year that The millage is levied.

c.title: MARION TOWNSHIP
c.q:
This millage will allow Marion Township to levy up to 1.5 mills ($1.50 per $1,000.00) to provide funds for road-related capital improvements and maintenance activities.

Shall Marion Township, Charlevoix County, Michigan, be authorized to levy an additional tax up to1.5 mills ($1.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) for a period of three (3) years, beginning with the 2026 tax levy and continuing through the 2028 tax levy, inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the construction, reconstruction, repair, resurfacing, preservation, maintenance, paving, graveling, engineering, drainage improvements, culvert replacement, shoulder improvements, signage, traffic control devices, rights-of-way improvements, and other lawful improvements to public roads located within or serving Marion Township?

It is estimated that 1.5 mills would raise approximately $203,789.89 in the first year the millage is levied (2026).

c.title: CITY OF CHARLEVOIX
c.q: Shall Article II Section 2.4 Council – Terms, Article IV Section 4.8 Election of Council Members of the City Charter, and Article XIV Initial Election and Terms of Office be amended to increase the term for each Council member from 2 years to 4 years?

c.title: CHARLEVOIX PUBLIC SCHOOLS
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, required for the school district to receive its revenue per pupil foundation allowance.

Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Charlevoix Public Schools, Charlevoix and Antrim Counties, Michigan, be increased by 3 mills ($3.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 2 years, 2027 and 2028, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 0.1981 mill is levied in 2027 is approximately $145,463 (this millage is to restore millage lost as a result of the reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will be levied only to the extent necessary to restore that reduction)?

c.title: ST. JAMES TOWNSHIP FIRE PROTECTION MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q:
This proposal reestablishes the 1.0 mills for fire protection, which was previously approved by the electors and expired after the December 2025 levy. Specifically, the proposal renews the previously authorized 0.9634 mills and restores the 0.0366 mills rolled back by the Headlee Amendment.

“Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution in St. James Township of 1.0 mills ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 0.9634 mills ($0.9634 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at and increased up to the original voted 1.0 mills ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for four (4) years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for fire protection, which 1.0 mills will raise an estimated $67,993 in the first year the millage is levied?”

c.title: ST. JAMES TOWNSHIP STREET AND ROADS MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q:
This proposal renews a millage for street and road construction and maintenance, previously approved by the electors that expired after the December 2025 levy. The original millage was 2.0 mills, reduced to 1.9268 mills by required rollbacks. This proposal renews the previously authorized millage, but only up to 1.2500 mills, not the original 2.0 mills.

“Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution in St. James Township, of 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 1.9268 mills ($1.9268 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at up to 1.2500 mills ($1.25 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for four years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for road construction and maintenance, which 1.2500 mills will raise an estimated $84,991 in the first year the millage is levied?”

c.title: ST. JAMES TOWNSHIP MEDICAL CENTER MILLAGE RENEWAL
c.q:
This proposal renews the 2.0 mill island medical center millage previously approved by the electors that expired after the December 2025 levy. Specifically, the proposal renews the previously authorized 1.9268 mills and restores the 0.0732 mills rolled back by the Headlee Amendment.

“Shall the previous voted increase in the tax limitations imposed under Article IX, Sec 6 of the Michigan Constitution in St. James Township of 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value), reduced to 1.9268 mills ($1.9268 per $1,000 of taxable value) by the required millage rollbacks, be renewed at and increased up to the original voted 2.0 mills ($2.00 per $1,000 of taxable value) and levied for four (4) years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the operation of Beaver Island’s medical center, which 2.0 mills will raise an estimated $135,986 in the first year the millage is levied?”

c.title: ST. JAMES TOWNSHIP MEDICAL CENTER MILLAGE INCREASE
c.q:
This proposal provides an additional 0.5 mills for operation of Beaver Island’s medical center.

“Shall St. James Township impose an increase of up to 0.5 mills ($0.50 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for four (4) years, 2026 through 2029 inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the operation of Beaver Island’s medical center, which 0.5-mill increase will raise an estimated $33,996 in the first year the millage is levied?”

c.title: HISTORICAL SOCIETY MILLAGE PROPOSAL
c.q:
The Township currently levies 0.2457 mills (originally 0.25 mills, rolled back by the Headlee Amendment) to support the Beaver Island Historical Society. This proposal would authorize an additional 0.2543 mills, bringing the total levy for the Historical Society to 0.5 mills.

“Shall St. James Township impose an increase of up to 0.2543 mills ($0.2543 per $1,000 of taxable value) in the tax limitation imposed under Article IX, Sec. 6 of the Michigan Constitution and levy it for two (2) years, 2026 through 2027 inclusive, for the purpose of providing funds for the Beaver Island Historical Society, which 0.2543-mills increase will raise an estimated $17,290 in the first year the millage is levied?”

c.title: BOYNE VALLEY TOWNSHIP
c.pre: AMBULANCE AND RESCUE SERVICE NEW ADDITIONAL MILLAGE
c.q: Boyne Valley Township seeks to authorize the levy of a new additional millage to fund ambulance and rescue services within its boundaries at a rate of one mill ($1.00 per $1,000 of taxable value of your real and personal property). The millage is proposed to be levied for up to two years, from 2026 to 2027. If approved, the Township would raise approximately $244,000.00 for ambulance and rescue services in the first year levied. Should the Township adopt this new additional millage?

c.title: Village of Boyne Falls Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance
c.q:
IT IS HEREBY ORDAINED BY THE PEOPLE OF THE VILLAGE OF BOYNE FALLS THAT:

Section 1. The title of this ordinance shall be the "Village of Boyne Falls Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance."

Section 2. Marihuana Establishments Prohibited. Marihuana establishments, as defined by MCL 333.27953(1), are prohibited within the boundaries of the Village of Boyne Falls.

Shall the "The Village of Boyne Falls Prohibition of Marihuana Establishments Ordinance" be approved?

c.title: BOYNE FALLS PUBLIC SCHOOL
c.q:
This proposal will allow the school district to continue to levy the statutory rate of not to exceed 18 mills on all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law. The remaining 4 mills are only available to be levied to restore millage lost as a reduction required by the Michigan Constitution of 1963 and will only be levied to the extent necessary to restore that reduction.

Shall the limitation on the amount of taxes which may be assessed against all property, except principal residence and other property exempted by law, in Boyne Falls Public School, Charlevoix and Antrim Counties, Michigan, be increased by 22 mills ($22.00 on each $1,000 of taxable valuation) for a period of 12 years, 2026 to 2037, inclusive, to provide funds for operating purposes; the estimate of the revenue the school district will collect if the millage is approved and 18 mills are levied in 2026 is approximately $3,552,662?
